newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia 96 sugar output 5.4 mt, headed up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia 96 sugar output 5.4 mt, headed up.

text.p: Australia's raw sugar production rose to 5.4 million tonnes 94 net titre in 1996 from 5.0 million tonnes in 1995, John Desmarchelier, general manager of the Australian Sugar Milling Council, said on Thursday.
Sugar cane production was headed for further growth in 1997 after last year's record production, he told Reuters.
Growing demand for land by Australian canegrowers reflected long-term confidence in the raw sugar industry, he said.
Desmarchelier was commenting on a 4.7 percent increase to more than 500,000 hectares in assigned land for canegrowing in Queensland, which produces almost all of Austalia's sugar crop.
Recent rains had improved the outlook for sugar cane production in the 1997 season, he also said.
Last season Australian sugar millers crushed a record 39.9 million tonnes of cane to post the fifth successive record Australian cane harvest and crushing season.
The increase of 22,645 hectares in land assigned for growing cane in Queensland brings the total assigned area in the state to 506,000 hectares.

The expansion in cane area also involves other states, with the New South Wales harvesting area rising by 4,000 ha over the last decade and cane now being commercially harvested in the Ord region of Western Australia, he said.
Between 1990 and 1996, the area assigned for cane growing in Queensland had increased by 112,000 ha or 30 percent, he said.
The 1997 expansion could have been more than seven percent if all mill areas last year had been able to agree on demand for new land, Desmarchelier said.
